notes: Auth: the firebase CLI login (a project owner), so beginTransaction gives a PESSIMISTIC read-write transaction and security rules do not apply; end-user behaviour is not recorded here.
Times, durations and transaction ids are replaced by placeholders (normalise in lib.mjs, and the replace maps of record-f2.mjs); everything else is as returned.

"items" in the descriptions is the subcollection aruma-ref-f2-lock-items and "others" is aruma-ref-f2-lock-others (unique ids, so the collection-group query reads only this run's documents); p1 and p2 are documents of aruma-ref-f2-lock that are never written themselves.

Each scenario: T1 begins read-write and runs the query in its transaction; then a commit without transaction sends the write. If the write has not returned after 6000 ms, T1 is rolled back. outcome says whether the write returned before T1 ended; writeEndedAfterRollbackMs is how long after the rollback returned it completed. Latencies include about 0.3-1 s of network.
Two runs of every scenario, run 2 after run 1, so documents inserted by run 1 are present in run 2.
